title: Tecnologia e futuro
sub: Will, going to, future continuous, may e might - cosa succederà
grammar: Futuro: will / going to / present continuous, future continuous, may e might per le possibilità

lessons.title: Parlare del futuro
lessons.intro: In italiano il futuro si dice spesso con il presente: «domani vado a Roma». In inglese devi scegliere tra will, going to e present continuous, e c'è anche il future continuous. Qui metti ordine.

steps.title: Will, going to, present continuous: ripasso
steps.body:
- **will + base**: decisioni prese **al momento di parlare**, promesse, offerte, previsioni basate su opinione (I think...). «The phone's ringing. **I'll get it.**»
- **going to + base**: **piani e intenzioni** già decisi; previsioni basate su **qualcosa che vedi**. «I'**m going to buy** a new laptop.» / «Look at those clouds! It's **going to rain**.»
- **present continuous**: **accordi già presi** con un tempo preciso. «We'**re meeting** the client at ten.»
- **present simple**: **orari e programmi fissi**. «The train **leaves** at 6.42.»

**Errore tipico degli italiani**: usare il presente per le offerte («Wait, I carry it for you») invece di will.
ex: It's heavy. I'll help you with that.
È pesante. Ti do una mano.
She's going to start a new job in May.
Inizierà un nuovo lavoro a maggio.
We're flying to Lisbon on Friday.
Voliamo a Lisbona venerdì.

steps.title: Future continuous: sarò in mezzo a un'azione
steps.body:
**Will be + verbo in -ing** descrive un'azione **in corso in un momento preciso del futuro**.
- This time tomorrow I'**ll be flying** to Madrid. (alle 12 di domani sono in volo)
- Don't call at nine: we'**ll be having** dinner.

Si usa anche per chiedere con cortesia dei programmi altrui: «**Will you be using** the car tonight?» (non vuol dire «hai intenzione di», chiede solo cosa succede).

Negativa: **won't be + -ing**. Domanda: **Will you be + -ing?**
table: Will you be using the laptop?
ex: At eight tomorrow I'll be sitting in a meeting.
Domani alle otto sarò in riunione.
Will you be using the printer this afternoon?
Userai la stampante questo pomeriggio?

steps.title: May, might, could: possibilità
steps.body:
Per dire che qualcosa è **possibile ma non certo** si usa **may / might / could + verbo base**.
- I **might go** to the party. (forse ci vado)
- It **may rain** later.
- The battery **could** run out before we get there.

**May** e **might** sono quasi uguali; might è un po' meno sicuro. La negativa è **may not / might not** (mai «mayn't» nell'uso normale; **could not** invece vuol dire impossibile).

**Errori tipici**: «I might to go», «I don't might go», «Maybe I will might...».

Attenzione: **maybe** (un solo avverbio) apre la frase; **may be** (due parole) è il verbo: «Maybe it will rain» / «It may be late».
ex: I might not have time to call you.
Forse non avrò tempo di chiamarti.
Maybe I'll buy a new phone next month.
Forse il mese prossimo comprerò un telefono nuovo.

steps.title: Dopo when, as soon as, if, before, until: il presente
steps.body:
Nelle frasi che parlano del futuro, dopo **when, as soon as, before, after, until, if** si usa il **present simple**, mai will.
- **As soon as I get** home, I'll send you the file.
- I'll wait **until you finish**.
- **If it rains**, we'll stay at home.

In italiano diciamo «quando arriverò» (futuro); in inglese **when I arrive**.

**Errore tipico**: «When I will arrive, I'll call you».
ex: I'll text you as soon as the train arrives.
Ti scrivo appena arriva il treno.
Before you leave, please back up your files.
Prima di andare, fai il backup dei file.

lessons.title: La casa intelligente
lessons.intro: Un blog sulla domotica: vantaggi, problemi e dubbi di chi non è ancora convinto. Nel testo trovi molte forme di futuro e di possibilità.

steps.title: Is a smart home really smarter?
steps.text:
Last week my brother installed a so-called smart home system in his flat. The lights, the heating and even the coffee machine are now controlled by an app. When I visited on Sunday, he was very proud. "In ten years," he told me, "every home will have one." I'm not so sure.

I admit that the idea is attractive. You may be stuck in traffic, but your heating will already be warming up the living room, and by the time you arrive the lights will be on. My brother says he's going to save about thirty pounds a month on energy bills. Experts agree that homes like his might use up to a fifth less electricity.

However, there are some problems. First of all, it all depends on your internet connection. On Sunday afternoon my brother's wifi dropped for ten minutes and suddenly nothing worked: the lights wouldn't turn on and the heating switched itself off. Then there is the question of privacy. A smart speaker is listening all the time, waiting to hear its name, and nobody can be completely sure where the recordings go. Finally, there is the cost. The system cost him nearly eight hundred pounds, and he will need to pay for updates every year.

Technology will probably keep changing our houses, but I think we should take it slowly. Next month I'm going to try a smart light bulb, which costs only ten pounds. If I like it, I may buy a few more. If not, I'll go back to the old switch, which has never crashed, never needed an update and never asked for my password. Perhaps in twenty years I'll be sitting in a house that answers my questions, and I'll wonder why I was so suspicious. But for now, I prefer to be in charge.

qs.q: What does the writer think about the idea that every home will be smart in ten years?
What can the heating do while the owner is stuck in traffic?
qs.why: «Your heating will already be warming up the living room».

qs.q: The writer's brother expects to save about ___ pounds a month.

opts: The wifi stopped working for a while.
qs.why: «My brother's wifi dropped for ten minutes and suddenly nothing worked».

qs.q: The writer is sure that the recordings of the smart speaker are safe.
qs.why: «Nobody can be completely sure where the recordings go».

qs.q: What is the writer going to do next month?
qs.why: «Next month I'm going to try a smart light bulb».

qs.q: The writer's brother has already bought a smart speaker.
qs.why: Si parla di smart speaker in generale, non si dice che il fratello ne abbia uno.

steps.q: Nel testo, «it all depends on your internet connection» significa:
opts: tutto dipende dalla connessione a internet

steps.s: Nobody can be completely ___ where the data goes.
steps.why: Be sure about / where = essere certi. Safe e secure descrivono la protezione, non la certezza.

steps.why: Energy bills = le bollette.

lessons.title: Come vivremo nel 2035?
lessons.intro: Un'intervista a una ricercatrice che studia come la tecnologia cambierà la vita quotidiana. Ascolta le previsioni e distingui ciò che è certo da ciò che è solo possibile.

steps.title: Tech Talk
steps.it: Ascolta l'intervista e rispondi. Puoi riascoltarla e usare la velocità lenta.
lines: Welcome to Tech Talk. With me today is Dr Priya Patel, who studies how technology changes our daily lives. Priya, what will we be doing in ten years' time?
Well, nobody knows for sure, but I think we'll be talking to our devices much more than typing. Most people won't carry a separate laptop and phone. They might use one small device for everything.
And what about cars? Will we still be driving them?

In big cities, probably not. By 2035 many cars will be driving themselves, so people will be reading or answering emails during their journey. But in the countryside, drivers may still be the majority.
Some of our listeners are worried about their jobs.

That's fair. Some jobs will disappear, that's true. But new ones will appear. Ten years ago nobody was working as a social media manager, and now thousands of people are. I'm not saying it will be easy, though. Workers will need to keep learning new skills.
What's your own plan? Are you going to buy any of this new technology?
Funny you ask! I'm going to try a smart watch next month, but I might not wear it for long. I'm not a big fan of being told to stand up every hour!

Many people might use one small ___ for everything.
By 2035, what will many people do during car journeys?

What does Priya say about jobs?

lessons.title: All'assistenza tecnica
lessons.intro: Il portatile si blocca e chiami l'assistenza: come descrivere il problema, dire cosa hai già provato e chiedere istruzioni senza perdere la pazienza.

steps.title: Spiegare il problema
steps.body:
- **I'm calling about** my laptop. / **I'm having a problem with** the wifi.
- **It keeps freezing / crashing** (continua a bloccarsi).
- **It started happening after the update.**
- **I've already tried** restarting it / resetting the router.
- **Nothing has changed.** / **It still doesn't work.**
- **My reference number is...** (il numero della pratica)

L'assistenza ti risponderà con: **Could you tell me what error message you're getting?** o **Can I take your name and number, please?**
ex: It keeps freezing every time I open the program.
Si blocca ogni volta che apro il programma.
I've already tried restarting it, but nothing has changed.
Ho già provato a riavviarlo, ma non è cambiato niente.

steps.title: Farsi guidare, con cortesia
steps.body:
- **Could you walk me through it, step by step?** = Può guidarmi passo dopo passo?
- **Sorry, could you repeat that?** / **Could you spell that for me?**
- **Hold on a moment, I'll just write that down.**
- **I'll be waiting by the computer.**
- **If that doesn't work, what should I do?**

Troppo diretto: «Tell me how to fix it.» Meglio: **Could you tell me how to fix it?** Per ringraziare: **Thank you for your help, that's really useful.**
ex: Could you walk me through it, step by step?
Può guidarmi passo dopo passo?
I'll be waiting by the computer.
Aspetterò davanti al computer.

lessons.title: Un'email per chiedere supporto
lessons.intro: Scriverai un'email di tono formale al servizio clienti per un prodotto che non funziona. Prima esercizi su aperture, chiusure e frasi cortesi.

steps.title: Come è fatta un'email di reclamo o di richiesta
steps.body:
- **Apertura**: Dear Sir or Madam, (non sai il nome) / Dear Mr Evans, (lo sai)
- **Motivo**: I'm writing about... / I'm writing to ask for help with...
- **Il problema**: Unfortunately, ... / It keeps freezing...
- **Cosa hai già provato**: I have already restarted it...
- **La richiesta**: Could you tell me...? / I was wondering if you could...
- **Disponibilità**: I'll be at home after six.
- **Chiusura**: I look forward to hearing from you. + **Yours faithfully,** (Dear Sir or Madam) / **Yours sincerely,** (Dear Mr Evans)

Il tono è formale: niente contrazioni troppo colloquiali, niente «Hi». Ricorda: **I look forward to hearing** (con -ing).
ex: I'm writing about the tablet I bought last week.
Scrivo riguardo al tablet che ho comprato la settimana scorsa.
I was wondering if you could help me.
Mi chiedevo se potesse aiutarmi.

steps.why: I'm writing about + argomento.

steps.s: I look forward to hear from you.
answers: I look forward to hearing from you
steps.why: In look forward to, to è una preposizione: serve -ing.

steps.s1: Could you please tell me how to reset the password?
steps.s2: I ___ you could tell me how to reset the password.
steps.why: I was wondering if... è una forma molto cortese per chiedere.

steps.s: Dear Sir or Madam, ... Yours ___ ,
steps.why: Dear Sir or Madam finisce con Yours faithfully; con il nome (Dear Mr Evans) si usa Yours sincerely.

steps.q: You bought a new tablet from an online shop two weeks ago. It has a problem. Write an email to the customer service. Explain what the problem is, say what you have already tried, ask for help, and say when you will be available.
steps.it: Scrivi un'email formale al servizio clienti: spiega il problema del tablet, cosa hai già provato, chiedi aiuto e dì quando sarai raggiungibile.
checklist: Ho aperto con Dear Sir or Madam e chiuso con Yours faithfully
Ho spiegato il problema con it keeps + -ing o simile
Ho detto che cosa ho già provato

Ho usato almeno una forma di futuro (will be, going to) e I look forward to hearing

steps.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I bought a tablet from your website two weeks ago. Unfortunately, it keeps freezing when I open the camera app, and sometimes the battery runs out in only two hours.

I have already restarted it and installed the latest update, but nothing has changed. I might have to return it, but first I would like to know if you can help me.

Could you tell me what I should do next? I will be at home every weekday after six, so you can phone me then. I'm also going to send you a short video of the problem.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Giulia Rossi

steps.q: Describe a technology problem you had recently and how you solved it.
steps.it: Racconta un problema tecnologico che hai avuto di recente e come l'hai risolto (almeno 4 frasi).
steps.model: Last week my phone froze and I couldn't turn it off. I tried to restart it, but nothing happened. In the end I held the button for ten seconds and it restarted. I was lucky because I had backed up my photos. Next time I'm going to update the system more carefully.

steps.q: Do you think you'll be using more or less technology in five years' time? Why?
steps.it: Pensi che tra cinque anni userai più o meno tecnologia? Perché? Usa will, going to, might (almeno 4 frasi).

steps.model: In five years' time I think I'll be using more technology, especially at work. I'll probably be working from home two days a week, so I'll need good software. But I might also spend less time on my phone, because I'm getting tired of social media. Perhaps I'll buy a smart watch, but I'm not sure yet.
